Compute calibrated RGB/proprioception geometry from saved permitted observations. request.kind selects camera/FK, rays, triangulation, pixel_plane intersections with a caller-assumed plane, point/path projection, tracking, batch (1..32 geometry queries in one call via queries=[...]) or explicitly reconstructed-scene queries. Prefer triangulate across two calibrated views (such as head and wrist) when a target feature is visible and matchable in both views, since it measures 3D position without assuming a plane height. Use pixel_plane on demand when a target or destination lies on a known support/table/container plane or when single-view occlusion/weak texture prevents reliable two-view matching: it returns a conditional point (not measured depth), d_point_d_normal_offset_m and cross_camera_projections in other calibrated views, plus optional plane_origin_alt_m sensitivity (assumption_delta_m) and optional target_camera_id overlay image; verify the plane hypothesis via cross_camera_projections or target_camera_id before choosing robot_action targets. Returns numerical value, source/quality/degeneracy evidence and projection images when applicable. build_scene returns a proposed patch without applying it or creating a saved scene_version; scene queries require an existing saved version. No native object truth, movement or physics rollout. Projection images are returned as independent image items. Depth kinds use the depth_query contract only when RGB-D is enabled. Compute calibrated RGB/proprioception geometry from saved permitted observations. request.kind selects camera/FK, rays, triangulation, pixel_plane intersections with a caller-assumed plane, point/path projection, tracking, batch (1..32 geometry queries in one call via queries=[...]) or explicitly reconstructed-scene queries. Prefer triangulate across two calibrated views (such as head and wrist) when a target feature is visible and matchable in both views, since it measures 3D position without assuming a plane height. Use pixel_plane on demand when a target or destination lies on a known support/table/container plane or when single-view occlusion/weak texture prevents reliable two-view matching: it returns a conditional point (not measured depth), d_point_d_normal_offset_m and cross_camera_projections in other calibrated views, plus optional plane_origin_alt_m sensitivity (assumption_delta_m) and optional target_camera_id overlay image; verify the plane hypothesis via cross_camera_projections or target_camera_id before choosing robot_action targets. Returns numerical value, source/quality/degeneracy evidence and projection images when applicable. build_scene returns a proposed patch without applying it or creating a saved scene_version; scene queries require an existing saved version. No native object truth, movement or physics rollout. Projection images are returned as independent image items. Depth kinds use the depth_query contract only when RGB-D is enabled. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"request":{"camera_id":"cam_head","kind":"pixel_ray","observation_id":"obs_1","pixel":[320,240]}}

pool:
Compute calibrated RGB/proprioception geometry from saved permitted observations. request.kind selects camera/FK, rays, triangulation, pixel_plane intersections with a caller-assumed plane, point/path projection, tracking, batch (1..32 geometry queries in one call via queries=[...]) or explicitly reconstructed-scene queries. Prefer triangulate across two calibrated views (such as head and wrist) when a target feature is visible and matchable in both views, since it measures 3D position without assuming a plane height. Use pixel_plane on demand when a target or destination lies on a known support/table/container plane or when single-view occlusion/weak texture prevents reliable two-view matching: it returns a conditional point (not measured depth), d_point_d_normal_offset_m and cross_camera_projections in other calibrated views, plus optional plane_origin_alt_m sensitivity (assumption_delta_m) and optional target_camera_id overlay image; verify the plane hypothesis via cross_camera_projections or target_camera_id before choosing robot_action targets. Returns numerical value, source/quality/degeneracy evidence and projection images when applicable. build_scene returns a proposed patch without applying it or creating a saved scene_version; scene queries require an existing saved version. No native object truth, movement or physics rollout. Projection images are returned as independent image items. Depth kinds use the depth_query contract only when RGB-D is enabled. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"request":{"camera_id":"cam_head","kind":"pixel_ray","observation_id":"obs_1","pixel":[320,240]}}

Compute calibrated RGB/proprioception geometry from saved permitted observations. request.kind selects camera/FK, rays, triangulation, pixel_plane intersections with a caller-assumed plane, point/path projection, tracking, batch (1..32 geometry queries in one call via queries=[...]) or explicitly reconstructed-scene queries. Prefer triangulate across two calibrated views (such as head and wrist) when a target feature is visible and matchable in both views, since it measures 3D position without assuming a plane height. Use pixel_plane on demand when a target or destination lies on a known support/table/container plane or when single-view occlusion/weak texture prevents reliable two-view matching: it returns a conditional point (not measured depth), d_point_d_normal_offset_m and cross_camera_projections in other calibrated views, plus optional plane_origin_alt_m sensitivity (assumption_delta_m) and optional target_camera_id overlay image; verify the plane hypothesis via cross_camera_projections or target_camera_id before choosing robot_action targets. Returns numerical value, source/quality/degeneracy evidence and projection images when applicable. build_scene returns a proposed patch without applying it or creating a saved scene_version; scene queries require an existing saved version. No native object truth, movement or physics rollout. Projection images are returned as independent image items. Depth kinds use the depth_query contract only when RGB-D is enabled. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"request":{"camera_id":"cam_head","kind":"pixel_ray","observation_id":"obs_1","pixel":[320,240]}}

pool:
Compute calibrated RGB/proprioception geometry from saved permitted observations. request.kind selects camera/FK, rays, triangulation, pixel_plane intersections with a caller-assumed plane, point/path projection, tracking, batch (1..32 geometry queries in one call via queries=[...]) or explicitly reconstructed-scene queries. Prefer triangulate across two calibrated views (such as head and wrist) when a target feature is visible and matchable in both views, since it measures 3D position without assuming a plane height. Use pixel_plane on demand when a target or destination lies on a known support/table/container plane or when single-view occlusion/weak texture prevents reliable two-view matching: it returns a conditional point (not measured depth), d_point_d_normal_offset_m and cross_camera_projections in other calibrated views, plus optional plane_origin_alt_m sensitivity (assumption_delta_m) and optional target_camera_id overlay image; verify the plane hypothesis via cross_camera_projections or target_camera_id before choosing robot_action targets. Returns numerical value, source/quality/degeneracy evidence and projection images when applicable. build_scene returns a proposed patch without applying it or creating a saved scene_version; scene queries require an existing saved version. No native object truth, movement or physics rollout. Projection images are returned as independent image items. Depth kinds use the depth_query contract only when RGB-D is enabled. In this run pixel_plane also accepts plane_source:'vggt', which replaces your plane height with an image-based estimate of the object's centre height at that pixel (alternate: its top); check value.plane_estimate.quality. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"request":{"camera_id":"cam_head","kind":"pixel_ray","observation_id":"obs_1","pixel":[320,240]}}

## Motion planning
robot_action is the common interface for arm and gripper motion. Default preview computes a whole batch
without moving: inspect costs, both arms' routes, jaw timing, supplied geometry and current RGB, then
execute its plan_id. Use explicit direct mode only when you choose to omit this review round trip.
An observe stage or optional checkpoint_after_gripper=true (on a grasp/gripper stage or batch) pauses both arms
at the stage boundary. Inspect the returned state, then resume the remaining stages with mode='execute' and the same plan_id
without replanning if still valid (do not re-submit already completed stages from the beginning);
when a stage fails or changed targets/routes require replanning from a stage boundary, pass source_plan_id and
start_from_stage_id (with optional stage_overrides) to recompile only the remaining stages. Execution never silently replans.
Completed stages report objective grip_facts (measured_jaw_before, measured_jaw_after, jaw_delta, measured_aperture_m,
aperture_delta_m; ARX-X5 full open is 0.088 m, closed is 0.0 m). Choose gripper verification from object properties:
for rigid objects of known thickness (blocks, bottles, tubes), prefer grip_guard_preset (rigid_object, wide_object, non_empty)
or custom min_aperture_m/max_aperture_m [0..0.088 m] on a closing jaw stage instead of an unconditional observe checkpoint,
so an empty grasp (~0.0 m) pauses automatically while a valid grasp continues uninterrupted into lift and placement;
for deformable/flexible or very thin objects (cloth corners, thin sheets/rims where a valid pinch closes nearly to 0.0 m),
avoid high aperture thresholds and use thin_object, none, or an explicit checkpoint_after_gripper=true only when visual
confirmation is needed before lifting or pulling; omit checkpoints for routine jaw opening or release-and-retract.
Match joint-travel bounds to the kinematic span of the maneuver: standard catches unintended 360° wrist winding on short moves;
when a maneuver intentionally rotates the wrist across a wide arc, flips an orientation, or sweeps/stretches a deformable object
across the workspace, set joint_travel_preset ('extended' or 'unconstrained') or custom max_joint_travel_rad/max_backtracking_rad.

## Run handoff policy
Choose whether a useful cross-arm transfer should use a stable physical support surface or a direct airborne handoff from current geometry, grasp stability, reachability, both-arm clearance and whole-task cost. Prefer an observed stable table/platform or other suitable physical support when practical; this is a recommendation, not a requirement to place the object down. Airborne handoff remains available when it better fits the visible conditions. Do not add a handoff when the holding arm can already deliver the object well. For supported transfer, lower and release onto sufficient footprint, inspect stable support, clear the giver, then regrasp with the receiver and verify a short lift. For airborne transfer, keep the giver supporting the object through receiver approach/close, inspect fresh evidence of receiver support before any separate giver release, and verify retention during separation. A closed jaw is insufficient. Simultaneous dual-arm movement, independent progression and per-arm queues remain available. Overlap work on different objects or independent preparation when swept volumes are clear; this handoff policy does not impose serial arms or a single-arm preference. Use existing move/gripper/queue tools and matching bounded templates; inspect current RGB between support-changing phases. This is a planning strategy, not a new motion Skill. Transfer preferences concern relocating an object between arms, for example when the working arm cannot reach it. For cooperative manipulation of one difficult object, such as stabilizing or orienting an irregular object, choose table-supported or airborne cooperation from current evidence with no inherent preference; a transfer preference does not prescribe the cooperation method.

## Motion planning
robot_action is the common interface for arm and gripper motion. Before choosing an arm or introducing a cross-arm
transfer, check whether ONE single arm can reach both source and destination (via preview or `s3.check_source_to_dest`,
as objects near the midline `|x| <= 0.18 m` are often directly deliverable by the destination-side arm with zero
handoff); when cross-arm transfer is physically required, follow the Run handoff policy. Match batch granularity to
physical uncertainty rather than fragmenting into 1-stage nudges: combine clear multi-stage manipulation sequences
(approach -> grasp -> lift -> transport -> place -> release -> withdraw) into one `robot_action` batch with conditional
`grip_guard_preset` and execute in a single turn via `robot_action(mode='execute_if_clean', plan_update={...},
observation_id=..., stages=[...])` (or `mode='direct'` / `program_run(allow_direct_actions=True)`). `execute_if_clean`
plans the full batch, checks kinematic/joint-limit `motion_safety` and any explicit `obstacle_object_ids`/`obstacles`,
and executes immediately when `blocking_risks` is empty while non-blocking `advisory_notes` do not block execution
(returning cached `plan_id` without moving if `blocking_risks` is non-empty). Pass `obstacle_object_ids=[...]` only for
non-target intermediate objects to route over/around (each listed ID becomes an observation-scoped solid world AABB
cuboid; never pass the target object or hollow racks, hooks, slots, or open containers being entered). Reserve two-turn `mode='preview'` -> `mode='execute'` for inspecting rendered
trajectory overlays when swept-arm clearance around complex 3D structures is genuinely ambiguous, and use zero-image
`mode='preflight'` (or `program_run`) for fast multi-candidate kinematic checks. Omit `image_delivery` on physical
`robot_action` calls so post-action `cam_head`, both close-range wrist RGB views, and trajectory feedback arrive
together automatically.
Omit redundant `observe` checkpoints on jaw opening, open-area release-and-retract, or at the end of a batch (every
physical `robot_action` already returns updated `cam_head`, both wrist RGB views, `grip_facts`, and `obs3d`). Stage
closed-loop visual verification right before high-precision contact: use `checkpoint_after_gripper=true` when
deformable sheet/edge co-motion is uncertain before lifting or folding, or place a single pre-entry `observe` stage at
hover/align (inspecting the close-range wrist RGB views or `robot_observe(focus_3d=...)` + two-view `triangulate`)
before sub-centimetre hole/slot/post/thread entry; resume with `mode='execute'` and the same `plan_id` if aligned, or
pass `source_plan_id` + `start_from_stage_id` (with `stage_overrides`) to recompile only the remaining stages.
Execution never silently replans.
Completed stages report objective `grip_facts` (`measured_jaw_before`, `measured_jaw_after`, `jaw_delta`,
`measured_aperture_m`, `aperture_delta_m`; ARX-X5 full open is 0.088 m, closed is 0.0 m). Match `grip_guard_preset` to
incompressible thickness: reserve `non_empty` (>=0.0015 m), `rigid_object` (>=0.002 m), and `wide_object` (>=0.003 m) strictly for incompressible
rigid blocks/cylinders >=8 mm thick so empty closures (~0.0 m) pause while valid grasps continue into lift; compressible
or soft items, thin items (<=4 mm), slender rods/tubes (<=8 mm), and deformable sheets pinch to 0.000–0.002 m, so use
`thin_object` (>=0.0005 m) or `none` to avoid false `aperture_below_min_m` pauses. When rotating an offset or heavy object
in mid-air, seat fingers deeper near its center of mass (`contact_region='finger_middle'` or positive `contact_depth_m`
when support clearance allows). On open-jaw grasp moves (`allow_jaw_symmetry=true` by default; set `false` when finger
polarity must stay fixed), the planner automatically resolves the exact 180° parallel-jaw twin if the primary branch hits
IK or wrist-winding limits (and resolves small contact-invariant approach tilts only when `allow_approach_tilt=true` is
opted in, reporting `resolved_angles_deg`), while closed-jaw/holding moves keep rigid orientation. Inside open-top containers,
keep `[0, 0, yaw]` vertical during descent/release when reachable so the forearm stays vertical above surrounding rims/flaps; when slanted/lateral
geometry or extended reaches constrain a top-down approach, use a 3D approach tilt (`[pitch, roll, yaw]`, e.g. via
`s3.solve_reachable_pose` / `s3.check_source_to_dest` or `allow_approach_tilt=true`). When withdrawing from a narrow slot or housing,
retract clear along the entry axis before opening the jaws wide so open fingers do not snag surrounding walls. For repetitive
multi-cycle operations, pack multiple cycles into one `robot_action` batch (up to 32 stages) or run verified loops in
`program_run` at normal speed to conserve step and turn budgets. Match joint-travel bounds to the maneuver: `standard`
catches unintended 360° wrist winding on short moves; set `joint_travel_preset` (`'extended'` or `'unconstrained'`) or
custom `max_joint_travel_rad`/`max_backtracking_rad` when wide-arc sweeps, large orientation flips, or deformable
stretches are intentional; if final return to initial `obs_1['robot_state']` flange poses hits `path_infeasible` from a
rotated posture, use `s3.plan_joint_safe_return` (`safe_transition_stages`).

physical uncertainty rather than fragmenting into 1-stage nudges: combine clear multi-stage manipulation sequences

`grip_guard_preset` and execute in a single turn via `robot_action(mode='execute_if_clean', plan_update={...},
observation_id=..., stages=[...])` (or `mode='direct'` / `program_run(allow_direct_actions=True)`). `execute_if_clean`
plans the full batch, checks kinematic/joint-limit `motion_safety` and any explicit `obstacle_object_ids`/`obstacles`,
and executes immediately when `blocking_risks` is empty while non-blocking `advisory_notes` do not block execution
(returning cached `plan_id` without moving if `blocking_risks` is non-empty). Pass `obstacle_object_ids=[...]` only for
non-target intermediate objects to route over/around (each listed ID becomes an observation-scoped solid world AABB
cuboid; never pass the target object or hollow racks, hooks, slots, or open containers being entered). Reserve two-turn `mode='preview'` -> `mode='execute'` for inspecting rendered
trajectory overlays when swept-arm clearance around complex 3D structures is genuinely ambiguous, and use zero-image
`mode='preflight'` (or `program_run`) for fast multi-candidate kinematic checks. Omit `image_delivery` on physical
`robot_action` calls so post-action `cam_head`, both close-range wrist RGB views, and trajectory feedback arrive
together automatically.

physical `robot_action` already returns updated `cam_head`, both wrist RGB views, `grip_facts`, and `obs3d`). Stage
closed-loop visual verification right before high-precision contact: use `checkpoint_after_gripper=true` when
deformable sheet/edge co-motion is uncertain before lifting or folding, or place a single pre-entry `observe` stage at
hover/align (inspecting the close-range wrist RGB views or `robot_observe(focus_3d=...)` + two-view `triangulate`)
before sub-centimetre hole/slot/post/thread entry; resume with `mode='execute'` and the same `plan_id` if aligned, or
pass `source_plan_id` + `start_from_stage_id` (with `stage_overrides`) to recompile only the remaining stages.

## Motion planning
robot_action is the common interface for arm and gripper motion. Before choosing an arm or introducing a cross-arm
transfer, check whether ONE single arm can reach both source and destination (via preview or `s3.check_source_to_dest`,
as objects near the midline `|x| <= 0.18 m` are often directly deliverable by the destination-side arm with zero
handoff); when cross-arm transfer is physically required, follow the Run handoff policy. Match batch granularity to
physical uncertainty rather than fragmenting into 1-stage nudges: combine clear multi-stage manipulation sequences
(approach -> grasp -> lift -> transport -> place -> release -> withdraw) into one `robot_action` batch with conditional
`grip_guard_preset` and execute in a single turn via `robot_action(mode='execute_if_clean', plan_update={...},
observation_id=..., stages=[...])` (or `mode='direct'` / `program_run(allow_direct_actions=True)`). `execute_if_clean`
plans the full batch, checks kinematic/joint-limit `motion_safety` and any explicit `obstacle_object_ids`/`obstacles`,
and executes immediately when `blocking_risks` is empty while non-blocking `advisory_notes` do not block execution
(returning cached `plan_id` without moving if `blocking_risks` is non-empty). Pass `obstacle_object_ids=[...]` only for
non-target intermediate objects to route over/around (each listed ID becomes an observation-scoped solid world AABB
cuboid; never pass the target object or hollow racks, hooks, slots, or open containers being entered). Reserve two-turn `mode='preview'` -> `mode='execute'` for inspecting rendered
trajectory overlays when swept-arm clearance around complex 3D structures is genuinely ambiguous, and use zero-image
`mode='preflight'` (or `program_run`) for fast multi-candidate kinematic checks. Omit `image_delivery` on physical
`robot_action` calls so post-action `cam_head`, both close-range wrist RGB views, and trajectory feedback arrive
together automatically.
Omit redundant `observe` checkpoints on jaw opening, open-area release-and-retract, or at the end of a batch (every
physical `robot_action` already returns updated `cam_head`, both wrist RGB views, `grip_facts`, and `obs3d`). Stage
closed-loop visual verification right before high-precision contact: use `checkpoint_after_gripper=true` when
deformable sheet/edge co-motion is uncertain before lifting or folding, or place a single pre-entry `observe` stage at
hover/align (inspecting the close-range wrist RGB views or `robot_observe(focus_3d=...)` + two-view `triangulate`)
before sub-centimetre hole/slot/post/thread entry; resume with `mode='execute'` and the same `plan_id` if aligned, or
pass `source_plan_id` + `start_from_stage_id` (with `stage_overrides`) to recompile only the remaining stages.
Execution never silently replans.
Completed stages report objective `grip_facts` (`measured_jaw_before`, `measured_jaw_after`, `jaw_delta`,
`measured_aperture_m`, `aperture_delta_m`; ARX-X5 full open is 0.088 m, closed is 0.0 m). Match `grip_guard_preset` to
incompressible thickness: reserve `non_empty` (>=0.0015 m), `rigid_object` (>=0.002 m), and `wide_object` (>=0.003 m) strictly for incompressible
rigid blocks/cylinders >=8 mm thick so empty closures (~0.0 m) pause while valid grasps continue into lift; compressible
or soft items, thin items (<=4 mm), slender rods/tubes (<=8 mm), and deformable sheets pinch to 0.000–0.002 m, so use
`thin_object` (>=0.0005 m) or `none` to avoid false `aperture_below_min_m` pauses. When rotating an offset or heavy object
in mid-air, seat fingers deeper near its center of mass (`contact_region='finger_middle'` or positive `contact_depth_m`
when support clearance allows). On open-jaw grasp moves (`allow_jaw_symmetry=true` by default; set `false` when finger
polarity must stay fixed), the planner automatically resolves the exact 180° parallel-jaw twin if the primary branch hits
IK or wrist-winding limits (and resolves small contact-invariant approach tilts only when `allow_approach_tilt=true` is
opted in, reporting `resolved_angles_deg`), while closed-jaw/holding moves keep rigid orientation. Inside open-top containers,
keep `[0, 0, yaw]` vertical during descent/release when reachable so the forearm stays vertical above surrounding rims/flaps; when slanted/lateral
geometry or extended reaches constrain a top-down approach, use a 3D approach tilt (`[pitch, roll, yaw]`, e.g. via
`s3.solve_reachable_pose` / `s3.check_source_to_dest` or `allow_approach_tilt=true`). When withdrawing from a narrow slot or housing,
retract clear along the entry axis before opening the jaws wide so open fingers do not snag surrounding walls. For repetitive
multi-cycle operations, pack multiple cycles into one `robot_action` batch (up to 32 stages) or run verified loops in

robot_action is the common interface for arm and gripper motion. Before choosing an arm or introducing a cross-arm

handoff); when cross-arm transfer is physically required, follow the Run handoff policy. Match batch granularity to
physical uncertainty rather than fragmenting into 1-stage nudges: combine clear multi-stage manipulation sequences
(approach -> grasp -> lift -> transport -> place -> release -> withdraw) into one `robot_action` batch with conditional
`grip_guard_preset` and execute in a single turn via `robot_action(mode='execute_if_clean', plan_update={...},
observation_id=..., stages=[...])` (or `mode='direct'` / `program_run(allow_direct_actions=True)`). `execute_if_clean`
plans the full batch, checks kinematic/joint-limit `motion_safety` and any explicit `obstacle_object_ids`/`obstacles`,
and executes immediately when `blocking_risks` is empty while non-blocking `advisory_notes` do not block execution
(returning cached `plan_id` without moving if `blocking_risks` is non-empty). Pass `obstacle_object_ids=[...]` only for
non-target intermediate objects to route over/around (each listed ID becomes an observation-scoped solid world AABB
cuboid; never pass the target object or hollow racks, hooks, slots, or open containers being entered). Reserve two-turn `mode='preview'` -> `mode='execute'` for inspecting rendered
trajectory overlays when swept-arm clearance around complex 3D structures is genuinely ambiguous, and use zero-image
`mode='preflight'` (or `program_run`) for fast multi-candidate kinematic checks. Omit `image_delivery` on physical
`robot_action` calls so post-action `cam_head`, both close-range wrist RGB views, and trajectory feedback arrive
together automatically.

physical `robot_action` already returns updated `cam_head`, both wrist RGB views, `grip_facts`, and `obs3d`). Stage
closed-loop visual verification right before high-precision contact: use `checkpoint_after_gripper=true` when
deformable sheet/edge co-motion is uncertain before lifting or folding, or place a single pre-entry `observe` stage at
hover/align (inspecting the close-range wrist RGB views or `robot_observe(focus_3d=...)` + two-view `triangulate`)
before sub-centimetre hole/slot/post/thread entry; resume with `mode='execute'` and the same `plan_id` if aligned, or
pass `source_plan_id` + `start_from_stage_id` (with `stage_overrides`) to recompile only the remaining stages.

robot_state, grip_facts, trajectory feedback, and inline 3D object_table/object_state_delta/scene3d when enabled).

sensor-resolution local crops on demand via robot_observe(focus_3d={'target_m': [x, y, z], 'radius_m': ...}) or

## Run handoff policy
Choose whether a useful cross-arm transfer should use a stable physical support surface or a direct airborne handoff from current geometry, grasp stability, reachability, both-arm clearance and whole-task cost. Prefer an observed stable table/platform or other suitable physical support when practical; this is a recommendation, not a requirement to place the object down. Airborne handoff remains available when it better fits the visible conditions. Do not add a handoff when the holding arm can already deliver the object well. For supported transfer, lower and release onto sufficient footprint, inspect stable support, clear the giver, then regrasp with the receiver and verify a short lift. For airborne transfer, keep the giver supporting the object through receiver approach/close, inspect fresh evidence of receiver support before any separate giver release, and verify retention during separation. A closed jaw is insufficient. Simultaneous dual-arm movement, independent progression and per-arm queues remain available. Overlap work on different objects or independent preparation when swept volumes are clear; this handoff policy does not impose serial arms or a single-arm preference. Use existing move/gripper/queue tools and matching bounded templates; inspect current RGB between support-changing phases. This is a planning strategy, not a new motion Skill. Transfer preferences concern relocating an object between arms, for example when the working arm cannot reach it. For cooperative manipulation of one difficult object, such as stabilizing or orienting an irregular object, choose table-supported or airborne cooperation from current evidence with no inherent preference; a transfer preference does not prescribe the cooperation method.

without moving: inspect costs, both arms' routes, jaw timing, supplied geometry and current RGB, then
execute its plan_id. Use explicit direct mode only when you choose to omit this review round trip.
An observe stage or optional checkpoint_after_gripper=true (on a grasp/gripper stage or batch) pauses both arms
at the stage boundary. Inspect the returned state, then resume the remaining stages with mode='execute' and the same plan_id
without replanning if still valid (do not re-submit already completed stages from the beginning);
when a stage fails or changed targets/routes require replanning from a stage boundary, pass source_plan_id and
start_from_stage_id (with optional stage_overrides) to recompile only the remaining stages. Execution never silently replans.

aperture_delta_m; ARX-X5 full open is 0.088 m, closed is 0.0 m). Choose gripper verification from object properties:
for rigid objects of known thickness (blocks, bottles, tubes), prefer grip_guard_preset (rigid_object, wide_object, non_empty)
or custom min_aperture_m/max_aperture_m [0..0.088 m] on a closing jaw stage instead of an unconditional observe checkpoint,
so an empty grasp (~0.0 m) pauses automatically while a valid grasp continues uninterrupted into lift and placement;
for deformable/flexible or very thin objects (cloth corners, thin sheets/rims where a valid pinch closes nearly to 0.0 m),
avoid high aperture thresholds and use thin_object, none, or an explicit checkpoint_after_gripper=true only when visual
confirmation is needed before lifting or pulling; omit checkpoints for routine jaw opening or release-and-retract.

when a maneuver intentionally rotates the wrist across a wide arc, flips an orientation, or sweeps/stretches a deformable object
across the workspace, set joint_travel_preset ('extended' or 'unconstrained') or custom max_joint_travel_rad/max_backtracking_rad.

Robot-model clearance and 2D overlays do not prove task-object clearance, contact, support or retention.

## Motion planning
robot_action is the common interface for arm and gripper motion. Before choosing an arm or introducing a cross-arm
transfer, check whether ONE single arm can reach both source and destination (via preview or `s3.check_source_to_dest`,
as objects near the midline `|x| <= 0.18 m` are often directly deliverable by the destination-side arm with zero
handoff); when cross-arm transfer is physically required, follow the Run handoff policy. Match batch granularity to
physical uncertainty rather than fragmenting into 1-stage nudges: combine clear multi-stage manipulation sequences
(approach -> grasp -> lift -> transport -> place -> release -> withdraw) into one `robot_action` batch with conditional
`grip_guard_preset` and execute in a single turn via `robot_action(mode='execute_if_clean', plan_update={...},
observation_id=..., stages=[...])` (or `mode='direct'` / `program_run(allow_direct_actions=True)`). `execute_if_clean`
plans the full batch, checks kinematic/joint-limit `motion_safety` and any explicit `obstacle_object_ids`/`obstacles`,
and executes immediately when `blocking_risks` is empty while non-blocking `advisory_notes` do not block execution
(returning cached `plan_id` without moving if `blocking_risks` is non-empty). Pass `obstacle_object_ids=[...]` only for
non-target intermediate objects to route over/around (each listed ID becomes an observation-scoped solid world AABB
cuboid; never pass the target object or hollow racks, hooks, slots, or open containers being entered). Reserve two-turn `mode='preview'` -> `mode='execute'` for inspecting rendered
trajectory overlays when swept-arm clearance around complex 3D structures is genuinely ambiguous, and use zero-image
`mode='preflight'` (or `program_run`) for fast multi-candidate kinematic checks. Omit `image_delivery` on physical
`robot_action` calls so post-action `cam_head`, both close-range wrist RGB views, and trajectory feedback arrive
together automatically.
Omit redundant `observe` checkpoints on jaw opening, open-area release-and-retract, or at the end of a batch (every
physical `robot_action` already returns updated `cam_head`, both wrist RGB views, `grip_facts`, and `obs3d`). Stage
closed-loop visual verification right before high-precision contact: use `checkpoint_after_gripper=true` when
deformable sheet/edge co-motion is uncertain before lifting or folding, or place a single pre-entry `observe` stage at
hover/align (inspecting the close-range wrist RGB views or `robot_observe(focus_3d=...)` + two-view `triangulate`)
before sub-centimetre hole/slot/post/thread entry; resume with `mode='execute'` and the same `plan_id` if aligned, or
pass `source_plan_id` + `start_from_stage_id` (with `stage_overrides`) to recompile only the remaining stages.
Execution never silently replans.
Completed stages report objective `grip_facts` (`measured_jaw_before`, `measured_jaw_after`, `jaw_delta`,
`measured_aperture_m`, `aperture_delta_m`; ARX-X5 full open is 0.088 m, closed is 0.0 m). Match `grip_guard_preset` to
incompressible thickness: reserve `non_empty` (>=0.0015 m), `rigid_object` (>=0.002 m), and `wide_object` (>=0.003 m) strictly for incompressible
rigid blocks/cylinders >=8 mm thick so empty closures (~0.0 m) pause while valid grasps continue into lift; compressible
or soft items, thin items (<=4 mm), slender rods/tubes (<=8 mm), and deformable sheets pinch to 0.000–0.002 m, so use
`thin_object` (>=0.0005 m) or `none` to avoid false `aperture_below_min_m` pauses. When rotating an offset or heavy object
in mid-air, seat fingers deeper near its center of mass (`contact_region='finger_middle'` or positive `contact_depth_m`
when support clearance allows). On open-jaw grasp moves (`allow_jaw_symmetry=true` by default; set `false` when finger
polarity must stay fixed), the planner automatically resolves the exact 180° parallel-jaw twin if the primary branch hits
IK or wrist-winding limits (and resolves small contact-invariant approach tilts only when `allow_approach_tilt=true` is
opted in, reporting `resolved_angles_deg`), while closed-jaw/holding moves keep rigid orientation. Inside open-top containers,
keep `[0, 0, yaw]` vertical during descent/release when reachable so the forearm stays vertical above surrounding rims/flaps; when slanted/lateral
geometry or extended reaches constrain a top-down approach, use a 3D approach tilt (`[pitch, roll, yaw]`, e.g. via
`s3.solve_reachable_pose` / `s3.check_source_to_dest` or `allow_approach_tilt=true`). When withdrawing from a narrow slot or housing,
retract clear along the entry axis before opening the jaws wide so open fingers do not snag surrounding walls. For repetitive
multi-cycle operations, pack multiple cycles into one `robot_action` batch (up to 32 stages) or run verified loops in
`program_run` at normal speed to conserve step and turn budgets. Match joint-travel bounds to the maneuver: `standard`
catches unintended 360° wrist winding on short moves; set `joint_travel_preset` (`'extended'` or `'unconstrained'`) or
custom `max_joint_travel_rad`/`max_backtracking_rad` when wide-arc sweeps, large orientation flips, or deformable
stretches are intentional; if final return to initial `obs_1['robot_state']` flange poses hits `path_infeasible` from a
rotated posture, use `s3.plan_joint_safe_return` (`safe_transition_stages`).

(`position_m` + `quaternion_xyzw`) strictly for replaying saved measured `link6` `ee_pose` dicts (such as final return,
since `angles_deg=[0,0,0]` maps to `TOP_DOWN_QUAT_WXYZ=[0.5,-0.5,0.5,0.5]`, not identity quaternion).
Grasp targets describe the center BETWEEN opposing fingers at the selected contact section;
the tool converts its link6 offset once, so do not add a manual offset. angles_deg=[pitch,roll,yaw]
are extrinsic world x,y,z rotations from the top-down reference, not conventional absolute Euler angles.

Use independent jaw speed settings. Prefer normal clear transit and slower short contact approaches;
slower commands cost more native steps. during-motion jaw schedules are command timing, not contact detection.
Match arrival tolerances and stall guards to each stage's orthogonal contact physics:

## Coordinates and timing

(`position_m` + `quaternion_xyzw`) strictly for replaying saved measured `link6` `ee_pose` dicts (such as final return,
since `angles_deg=[0,0,0]` maps to `TOP_DOWN_QUAT_WXYZ=[0.5,-0.5,0.5,0.5]`, not identity quaternion).
Grasp targets describe the center BETWEEN opposing fingers at the selected contact section;
the tool converts its link6 offset once, so do not add a manual offset. angles_deg=[pitch,roll,yaw]
are extrinsic world x,y,z rotations from the top-down reference, not conventional absolute Euler angles.
[0,0,0] points tool +x down and opens the jaws along world -x. contact_region selects pad_center,
finger_middle or fingertip; contact_depth_m is the alternative depth toward the palm from pad_center.
An omitted arm speed uses this run's default; speed_preset and speed_scale are alternatives.
Use independent jaw speed settings. Prefer normal clear transit and slower short contact approaches;
slower commands cost more native steps. during-motion jaw schedules are command timing, not contact detection.
Match arrival tolerances and stall guards to each stage's orthogonal contact physics:
- `normal` (0.010 m, 0.15 rad, default): standard workspace moves, surface grasps (add `stall_guard_preset='contact_stop'` on low-clearance support descents `fingertip_support_clearance_m <= 0.010` m so real contact stops and holds pose while keeping `0.010` m planar centering), and loaded lift/transport/hover moves (pair `max_downward_dz_m` in `[0, 0.15]` m, e.g. `0.020–0.060` m, when held payload weight causes static joint-PD `-Z` gravity sag while horizontal `(dx, dy)` stays aligned).
- `tight` (0.003 m, 0.05 rad): millimeter free-space pre-entry or handoff alignment before contact (pair `max_downward_dz_m` if held payload weight causes static `-Z` gravity sag at alignment; avoid `tight` on physical contact seating where contact reaction torque deflects wrist PD).
- `compliant` (0.015 m, 0.20 rad, `max_upward_dz_m=0.040` m): contact seating and placing onto support where physical support stops Z above target (increase explicit `max_upward_dz_m` up to `0.15` m when deeper upward contact stop travel is expected; keep `normal` rather than `compliant` on small/thin grasps so a `+0.040` m window does not accept stopping above the object).
- `coarse` (0.025 m, 0.35 rad): unloaded transit, approach waypoints, post-release retraction, or compliant lateral travel (and
  `unconstrained_orientation` when wrist yaw is free).

## Feedback and next decision
Action results include actual completion/partial execution and the updated observation (RGB images, measured
robot_state, grip_facts, trajectory feedback, and inline 3D object_table/object_state_delta/scene3d when enabled).
Inspect that feedback before requesting another observation or correcting a target. Distinguish planned commands,
measured state, and your own object judgments; missing evidence remains unknown. After failure use actual state and
the completed range; do not replay completed work.
When sub-centimetre local geometry (insert holes, narrow slots, connector ports, elevated hooks) or
deformable cloth folds/corners require visual detail beyond coarse 3D boxes and 1 cm voxels, request 1:1 native
sensor-resolution local crops on demand via robot_observe(focus_3d={'target_m': [x, y, z], 'radius_m': ...}) or
robot_observe(focus_3d={'object_id': 'o2'}) (or zero-step history_view_observation(..., focus_3d={...})); after picking
[local_u, local_v] on a crop, convert back to full-frame pixel coordinates via
full_uv = [crop_xywh_px[0] + local_u, crop_xywh_px[1] + local_v] for direct use in geometry_query (triangulate /
pixel_plane) or s3.triangulate_rays.
For 3D localization with geometry_query, prefer triangulate across two calibrated views when a 3D object feature is
matchable in both; use pixel_plane on demand when a target/destination lies on a known support plane or single-view
occlusion prevents stereo matching (a single projected point on target_camera_id lies on the source ray and only tests
the assumed plane height along the cyan normal-offset band, so use plane_origin_alt_m or triangulate when object top vs
table height matters). Both triangulate and pixel_plane return gripper_relative (point_minus_grasp_world_m and
jaw_midplane_normal): for a held object or tool tip, subtract point_minus_grasp_world_m from the destination point to
compute the required grasp_position_m at the same gripper orientation.
The latest action receipt is already inline; in multi-step recovery or long episodes, use history_list_actions
with anchor='failures', 'gripper_commands' or 'events' on demand to compare earlier attempts and measured_delta.
Keep enough native-step budget for the remaining operation, verification and any task-required final return.
Images of historical frames retain historical state; current budgets are separately identified.
Use normal task progress to test your assumptions where possible: a useful approach, lift or withdrawal
can also provide evidence. Add a separate probe only if its answer changes the next decision and is not
available in existing feedback. Before a long batch, place an observation checkpoint only where later
stages depend on uncertain earlier outcomes; deterministic independent stages can stay together.

## Run handoff policy
Choose whether a useful cross-arm transfer should use a stable physical support surface or a direct airborne handoff from current geometry, grasp stability, reachability, both-arm clearance and whole-task cost. Prefer an observed stable table/platform or other suitable physical support when practical; this is a recommendation, not a requirement to place the object down. Airborne handoff remains available when it better fits the visible conditions. Do not add a handoff when the holding arm can already deliver the object well. For supported transfer, lower and release onto sufficient footprint, inspect stable support, clear the giver, then regrasp with the receiver and verify a short lift. For airborne transfer, keep the giver supporting the object through receiver approach/close, inspect fresh evidence of receiver support before any separate giver release, and verify retention during separation. A closed jaw is insufficient. Simultaneous dual-arm movement, independent progression and per-arm queues remain available. Overlap work on different objects or independent preparation when swept volumes are clear; this handoff policy does not impose serial arms or a single-arm preference. Use existing move/gripper/queue tools and matching bounded templates; inspect current RGB between support-changing phases. This is a planning strategy, not a new motion Skill. Transfer preferences concern relocating an object between arms, for example when the working arm cannot reach it. For cooperative manipulation of one difficult object, such as stabilizing or orienting an irregular object, choose table-supported or airborne cooperation from current evidence with no inherent preference; a transfer preference does not prescribe the cooperation method.

## Motion planning
robot_action is the common interface for arm and gripper motion. Default preview computes a whole batch
without moving: inspect costs, both arms' routes, jaw timing, supplied geometry and current RGB, then
execute its plan_id. Use explicit direct mode only when you choose to omit this review round trip.
An observe stage or optional checkpoint_after_gripper=true (on a grasp/gripper stage or batch) pauses both arms
at the stage boundary. Inspect the returned state, then resume the remaining stages with mode='execute' and the same plan_id
without replanning if still valid (do not re-submit already completed stages from the beginning);
when a stage fails or changed targets/routes require replanning from a stage boundary, pass source_plan_id and
start_from_stage_id (with optional stage_overrides) to recompile only the remaining stages. Execution never silently replans.
Completed stages report objective grip_facts (measured_jaw_before, measured_jaw_after, jaw_delta, measured_aperture_m,
aperture_delta_m; ARX-X5 full open is 0.088 m, closed is 0.0 m). Choose gripper verification from object properties:
for rigid objects of known thickness (blocks, bottles, tubes), prefer grip_guard_preset (rigid_object, wide_object, non_empty)
or custom min_aperture_m/max_aperture_m [0..0.088 m] on a closing jaw stage instead of an unconditional observe checkpoint,
so an empty grasp (~0.0 m) pauses automatically while a valid grasp continues uninterrupted into lift and placement;
for deformable/flexible or very thin objects (cloth corners, thin sheets/rims where a valid pinch closes nearly to 0.0 m),
avoid high aperture thresholds and use thin_object, none, or an explicit checkpoint_after_gripper=true only when visual
confirmation is needed before lifting or pulling; omit checkpoints for routine jaw opening or release-and-retract.
Match joint-travel bounds to the kinematic span of the maneuver: standard catches unintended 360° wrist winding on short moves;
when a maneuver intentionally rotates the wrist across a wide arc, flips an orientation, or sweeps/stretches a deformable object
across the workspace, set joint_travel_preset ('extended' or 'unconstrained') or custom max_joint_travel_rad/max_backtracking_rad.
Stages on each arm are ordered; depends_on adds cross-arm prerequisites. Independent work can overlap.
Robot-model clearance and 2D overlays do not prove task-object clearance, contact, support or retention.

## Motion planning
robot_action is the common interface for arm and gripper motion. Before choosing an arm or introducing a cross-arm
transfer, check whether ONE single arm can reach both source and destination (via preview or `s3.check_source_to_dest`,
as objects near the midline `|x| <= 0.18 m` are often directly deliverable by the destination-side arm with zero
handoff); when cross-arm transfer is physically required, follow the Run handoff policy. Match batch granularity to
physical uncertainty rather than fragmenting into 1-stage nudges: combine clear multi-stage manipulation sequences
(approach -> grasp -> lift -> transport -> place -> release -> withdraw) into one `robot_action` batch with conditional
`grip_guard_preset` and execute in a single turn via `robot_action(mode='execute_if_clean', plan_update={...},
observation_id=..., stages=[...])` (or `mode='direct'` / `program_run(allow_direct_actions=True)`). `execute_if_clean`
plans the full batch, checks kinematic/joint-limit `motion_safety` and any explicit `obstacle_object_ids`/`obstacles`,
and executes immediately when `blocking_risks` is empty while non-blocking `advisory_notes` do not block execution
(returning cached `plan_id` without moving if `blocking_risks` is non-empty). Pass `obstacle_object_ids=[...]` only for
non-target intermediate objects to route over/around (each listed ID becomes an observation-scoped solid world AABB
cuboid; never pass the target object or hollow racks, hooks, slots, or open containers being entered). Reserve two-turn `mode='preview'` -> `mode='execute'` for inspecting rendered
trajectory overlays when swept-arm clearance around complex 3D structures is genuinely ambiguous, and use zero-image
`mode='preflight'` (or `program_run`) for fast multi-candidate kinematic checks. Omit `image_delivery` on physical
`robot_action` calls so post-action `cam_head`, both close-range wrist RGB views, and trajectory feedback arrive
together automatically.
Omit redundant `observe` checkpoints on jaw opening, open-area release-and-retract, or at the end of a batch (every
physical `robot_action` already returns updated `cam_head`, both wrist RGB views, `grip_facts`, and `obs3d`). Stage
closed-loop visual verification right before high-precision contact: use `checkpoint_after_gripper=true` when
deformable sheet/edge co-motion is uncertain before lifting or folding, or place a single pre-entry `observe` stage at
hover/align (inspecting the close-range wrist RGB views or `robot_observe(focus_3d=...)` + two-view `triangulate`)
before sub-centimetre hole/slot/post/thread entry; resume with `mode='execute'` and the same `plan_id` if aligned, or
pass `source_plan_id` + `start_from_stage_id` (with `stage_overrides`) to recompile only the remaining stages.
Execution never silently replans.
Completed stages report objective `grip_facts` (`measured_jaw_before`, `measured_jaw_after`, `jaw_delta`,
`measured_aperture_m`, `aperture_delta_m`; ARX-X5 full open is 0.088 m, closed is 0.0 m). Match `grip_guard_preset` to
incompressible thickness: reserve `non_empty` (>=0.0015 m), `rigid_object` (>=0.002 m), and `wide_object` (>=0.003 m) strictly for incompressible
rigid blocks/cylinders >=8 mm thick so empty closures (~0.0 m) pause while valid grasps continue into lift; compressible
or soft items, thin items (<=4 mm), slender rods/tubes (<=8 mm), and deformable sheets pinch to 0.000–0.002 m, so use
`thin_object` (>=0.0005 m) or `none` to avoid false `aperture_below_min_m` pauses. When rotating an offset or heavy object
in mid-air, seat fingers deeper near its center of mass (`contact_region='finger_middle'` or positive `contact_depth_m`
when support clearance allows). On open-jaw grasp moves (`allow_jaw_symmetry=true` by default; set `false` when finger
polarity must stay fixed), the planner automatically resolves the exact 180° parallel-jaw twin if the primary branch hits
IK or wrist-winding limits (and resolves small contact-invariant approach tilts only when `allow_approach_tilt=true` is
opted in, reporting `resolved_angles_deg`), while closed-jaw/holding moves keep rigid orientation. Inside open-top containers,
keep `[0, 0, yaw]` vertical during descent/release when reachable so the forearm stays vertical above surrounding rims/flaps; when slanted/lateral
geometry or extended reaches constrain a top-down approach, use a 3D approach tilt (`[pitch, roll, yaw]`, e.g. via

## Coordinates and timing
Positions are metres in env_origin. Use `grasp_position_m` + `angles_deg` for all task poses; reserve raw EE targets
(`position_m` + `quaternion_xyzw`) strictly for replaying saved measured `link6` `ee_pose` dicts (such as final return,
since `angles_deg=[0,0,0]` maps to `TOP_DOWN_QUAT_WXYZ=[0.5,-0.5,0.5,0.5]`, not identity quaternion).

the tool converts its link6 offset once, so do not add a manual offset. angles_deg=[pitch,roll,yaw]
are extrinsic world x,y,z rotations from the top-down reference, not conventional absolute Euler angles.
[0,0,0] points tool +x down and opens the jaws along world -x. contact_region selects pad_center,
finger_middle or fingertip; contact_depth_m is the alternative depth toward the palm from pad_center.
An omitted arm speed uses this run's default; speed_preset and speed_scale are alternatives.

slower commands cost more native steps. during-motion jaw schedules are command timing, not contact detection.

## Coordinates and timing
Positions are metres in env_origin. Use `grasp_position_m` + `angles_deg` for all task poses; reserve raw EE targets
(`position_m` + `quaternion_xyzw`) strictly for replaying saved measured `link6` `ee_pose` dicts (such as final return,
since `angles_deg=[0,0,0]` maps to `TOP_DOWN_QUAT_WXYZ=[0.5,-0.5,0.5,0.5]`, not identity quaternion).
Grasp targets describe the center BETWEEN opposing fingers at the selected contact section;
the tool converts its link6 offset once, so do not add a manual offset. angles_deg=[pitch,roll,yaw]
are extrinsic world x,y,z rotations from the top-down reference, not conventional absolute Euler angles.
[0,0,0] points tool +x down and opens the jaws along world -x. contact_region selects pad_center,
finger_middle or fingertip; contact_depth_m is the alternative depth toward the palm from pad_center.
An omitted arm speed uses this run's default; speed_preset and speed_scale are alternatives.
Use independent jaw speed settings. Prefer normal clear transit and slower short contact approaches;
slower commands cost more native steps. during-motion jaw schedules are command timing, not contact detection.
Match arrival tolerances and stall guards to each stage's orthogonal contact physics:
- `normal` (0.010 m, 0.15 rad, default): standard workspace moves, surface grasps (add `stall_guard_preset='contact_stop'` on low-clearance support descents `fingertip_support_clearance_m <= 0.010` m so real contact stops and holds pose while keeping `0.010` m planar centering), and loaded lift/transport/hover moves (pair `max_downward_dz_m` in `[0, 0.15]` m, e.g. `0.020–0.060` m, when held payload weight causes static joint-PD `-Z` gravity sag while horizontal `(dx, dy)` stays aligned).

## Coordinates and timing
Positions are metres in env_origin. Use `grasp_position_m` + `angles_deg` for all task poses; reserve raw EE targets
(`position_m` + `quaternion_xyzw`) strictly for replaying saved measured `link6` `ee_pose` dicts (such as final return,
since `angles_deg=[0,0,0]` maps to `TOP_DOWN_QUAT_WXYZ=[0.5,-0.5,0.5,0.5]`, not identity quaternion).
Grasp targets describe the center BETWEEN opposing fingers at the selected contact section;
the tool converts its link6 offset once, so do not add a manual offset. angles_deg=[pitch,roll,yaw]
are extrinsic world x,y,z rotations from the top-down reference, not conventional absolute Euler angles.
[0,0,0] points tool +x down and opens the jaws along world -x. contact_region selects pad_center,
finger_middle or fingertip; contact_depth_m is the alternative depth toward the palm from pad_center.
An omitted arm speed uses this run's default; speed_preset and speed_scale are alternatives.
Use independent jaw speed settings. Prefer normal clear transit and slower short contact approaches;
slower commands cost more native steps. during-motion jaw schedules are command timing, not contact detection.
Match arrival tolerances and stall guards to each stage's orthogonal contact physics:
- `normal` (0.010 m, 0.15 rad, default): standard workspace moves, surface grasps (add `stall_guard_preset='contact_stop'` on low-clearance support descents `fingertip_support_clearance_m <= 0.010` m so real contact stops and holds pose while keeping `0.010` m planar centering), and loaded lift/transport/hover moves (pair `max_downward_dz_m` in `[0, 0.15]` m, e.g. `0.020–0.060` m, when held payload weight causes static joint-PD `-Z` gravity sag while horizontal `(dx, dy)` stays aligned).
- `tight` (0.003 m, 0.05 rad): millimeter free-space pre-entry or handoff alignment before contact (pair `max_downward_dz_m` if held payload weight causes static `-Z` gravity sag at alignment; avoid `tight` on physical contact seating where contact reaction torque deflects wrist PD).
- `compliant` (0.015 m, 0.20 rad, `max_upward_dz_m=0.040` m): contact seating and placing onto support where physical support stops Z above target (increase explicit `max_upward_dz_m` up to `0.15` m when deeper upward contact stop travel is expected; keep `normal` rather than `compliant` on small/thin grasps so a `+0.040` m window does not accept stopping above the object).
- `coarse` (0.025 m, 0.35 rad): unloaded transit, approach waypoints, post-release retraction, or compliant lateral travel (and
  `unconstrained_orientation` when wrist yaw is free).

## Coordinates and timing
Positions are metres in env_origin. Use `grasp_position_m` + `angles_deg` for all task poses; reserve raw EE targets
(`position_m` + `quaternion_xyzw`) strictly for replaying saved measured `link6` `ee_pose` dicts (such as final return,
since `angles_deg=[0,0,0]` maps to `TOP_DOWN_QUAT_WXYZ=[0.5,-0.5,0.5,0.5]`, not identity quaternion).
Grasp targets describe the center BETWEEN opposing fingers at the selected contact section;
the tool converts its link6 offset once, so do not add a manual offset. angles_deg=[pitch,roll,yaw]
are extrinsic world x,y,z rotations from the top-down reference, not conventional absolute Euler angles.
[0,0,0] points tool +x down and opens the jaws along world -x. contact_region selects pad_center,
finger_middle or fingertip; contact_depth_m is the alternative depth toward the palm from pad_center.
An omitted arm speed uses this run's default; speed_preset and speed_scale are alternatives.
Use independent jaw speed settings. Prefer normal clear transit and slower short contact approaches;
slower commands cost more native steps. during-motion jaw schedules are command timing, not contact detection.
Match arrival tolerances and stall guards to each stage's orthogonal contact physics:
- `normal` (0.010 m, 0.15 rad, default): standard workspace moves, surface grasps (add `stall_guard_preset='contact_stop'` on low-clearance support descents `fingertip_support_clearance_m <= 0.010` m so real contact stops and holds pose while keeping `0.010` m planar centering), and loaded lift/transport/hover moves (pair `max_downward_dz_m` in `[0, 0.15]` m, e.g. `0.020–0.060` m, when held payload weight causes static joint-PD `-Z` gravity sag while horizontal `(dx, dy)` stays aligned).
- `tight` (0.003 m, 0.05 rad): millimeter free-space pre-entry or handoff alignment before contact (pair `max_downward_dz_m` if held payload weight causes static `-Z` gravity sag at alignment; avoid `tight` on physical contact seating where contact reaction torque deflects wrist PD).

`robot_action` calls so post-action `cam_head`, both close-range wrist RGB views, and trajectory feedback arrive
together automatically.
Omit redundant `observe` checkpoints on jaw opening, open-area release-and-retract, or at the end of a batch (every
physical `robot_action` already returns updated `cam_head`, both wrist RGB views, `grip_facts`, and `obs3d`). Stage
closed-loop visual verification right before high-precision contact: use `checkpoint_after_gripper=true` when
deformable sheet/edge co-motion is uncertain before lifting or folding, or place a single pre-entry `observe` stage at
hover/align (inspecting the close-range wrist RGB views or `robot_observe(focus_3d=...)` + two-view `triangulate`)
before sub-centimetre hole/slot/post/thread entry; resume with `mode='execute'` and the same `plan_id` if aligned, or
pass `source_plan_id` + `start_from_stage_id` (with `stage_overrides`) to recompile only the remaining stages.
Execution never silently replans.
Completed stages report objective `grip_facts` (`measured_jaw_before`, `measured_jaw_after`, `jaw_delta`,
`measured_aperture_m`, `aperture_delta_m`; ARX-X5 full open is 0.088 m, closed is 0.0 m). Match `grip_guard_preset` to
incompressible thickness: reserve `non_empty` (>=0.0015 m), `rigid_object` (>=0.002 m), and `wide_object` (>=0.003 m) strictly for incompressible
rigid blocks/cylinders >=8 mm thick so empty closures (~0.0 m) pause while valid grasps continue into lift; compressible
or soft items, thin items (<=4 mm), slender rods/tubes (<=8 mm), and deformable sheets pinch to 0.000–0.002 m, so use
`thin_object` (>=0.0005 m) or `none` to avoid false `aperture_below_min_m` pauses. When rotating an offset or heavy object
in mid-air, seat fingers deeper near its center of mass (`contact_region='finger_middle'` or positive `contact_depth_m`
when support clearance allows). On open-jaw grasp moves (`allow_jaw_symmetry=true` by default; set `false` when finger
polarity must stay fixed), the planner automatically resolves the exact 180° parallel-jaw twin if the primary branch hits
IK or wrist-winding limits (and resolves small contact-invariant approach tilts only when `allow_approach_tilt=true` is
opted in, reporting `resolved_angles_deg`), while closed-jaw/holding moves keep rigid orientation. Inside open-top containers,
keep `[0, 0, yaw]` vertical during descent/release when reachable so the forearm stays vertical above surrounding rims/flaps; when slanted/lateral
geometry or extended reaches constrain a top-down approach, use a 3D approach tilt (`[pitch, roll, yaw]`, e.g. via
`s3.solve_reachable_pose` / `s3.check_source_to_dest` or `allow_approach_tilt=true`). When withdrawing from a narrow slot or housing,
retract clear along the entry axis before opening the jaws wide so open fingers do not snag surrounding walls. For repetitive
multi-cycle operations, pack multiple cycles into one `robot_action` batch (up to 32 stages) or run verified loops in
`program_run` at normal speed to conserve step and turn budgets. Match joint-travel bounds to the maneuver: `standard`
catches unintended 360° wrist winding on short moves; set `joint_travel_preset` (`'extended'` or `'unconstrained'`) or
custom `max_joint_travel_rad`/`max_backtracking_rad` when wide-arc sweeps, large orientation flips, or deformable
stretches are intentional; if final return to initial `obs_1['robot_state']` flange poses hits `path_infeasible` from a
rotated posture, use `s3.plan_joint_safe_return` (`safe_transition_stages`).
Stages on each arm are ordered; `depends_on` adds cross-arm prerequisites. Independent work can overlap.
Robot-model clearance and 2D overlays do not prove task-object clearance, contact, support or retention.

## Coordinates and timing
Positions are metres in env_origin. Use `grasp_position_m` + `angles_deg` for all task poses; reserve raw EE targets
(`position_m` + `quaternion_xyzw`) strictly for replaying saved measured `link6` `ee_pose` dicts (such as final return,
since `angles_deg=[0,0,0]` maps to `TOP_DOWN_QUAT_WXYZ=[0.5,-0.5,0.5,0.5]`, not identity quaternion).
Grasp targets describe the center BETWEEN opposing fingers at the selected contact section;
the tool converts its link6 offset once, so do not add a manual offset. angles_deg=[pitch,roll,yaw]
are extrinsic world x,y,z rotations from the top-down reference, not conventional absolute Euler angles.
[0,0,0] points tool +x down and opens the jaws along world -x. contact_region selects pad_center,
finger_middle or fingertip; contact_depth_m is the alternative depth toward the palm from pad_center.
An omitted arm speed uses this run's default; speed_preset and speed_scale are alternatives.
Use independent jaw speed settings. Prefer normal clear transit and slower short contact approaches;
slower commands cost more native steps. during-motion jaw schedules are command timing, not contact detection.
Match arrival tolerances and stall guards to each stage's orthogonal contact physics:
- `normal` (0.010 m, 0.15 rad, default): standard workspace moves, surface grasps (add `stall_guard_preset='contact_stop'` on low-clearance support descents `fingertip_support_clearance_m <= 0.010` m so real contact stops and holds pose while keeping `0.010` m planar centering), and loaded lift/transport/hover moves (pair `max_downward_dz_m` in `[0, 0.15]` m, e.g. `0.020–0.060` m, when held payload weight causes static joint-PD `-Z` gravity sag while horizontal `(dx, dy)` stays aligned).
- `tight` (0.003 m, 0.05 rad): millimeter free-space pre-entry or handoff alignment before contact (pair `max_downward_dz_m` if held payload weight causes static `-Z` gravity sag at alignment; avoid `tight` on physical contact seating where contact reaction torque deflects wrist PD).
- `compliant` (0.015 m, 0.20 rad, `max_upward_dz_m=0.040` m): contact seating and placing onto support where physical support stops Z above target (increase explicit `max_upward_dz_m` up to `0.15` m when deeper upward contact stop travel is expected; keep `normal` rather than `compliant` on small/thin grasps so a `+0.040` m window does not accept stopping above the object).
- `coarse` (0.025 m, 0.35 rad): unloaded transit, approach waypoints, post-release retraction, or compliant lateral travel (and
  `unconstrained_orientation` when wrist yaw is free).

## Feedback and next decision
Action results include actual completion/partial execution and the updated observation (RGB images, measured
robot_state, grip_facts, trajectory feedback, and inline 3D object_table/object_state_delta/scene3d when enabled).
Inspect that feedback before requesting another observation or correcting a target. Distinguish planned commands,
measured state, and your own object judgments; missing evidence remains unknown. After failure use actual state and
the completed range; do not replay completed work.
When sub-centimetre local geometry (insert holes, narrow slots, connector ports, elevated hooks) or
deformable cloth folds/corners require visual detail beyond coarse 3D boxes and 1 cm voxels, request 1:1 native
sensor-resolution local crops on demand via robot_observe(focus_3d={'target_m': [x, y, z], 'radius_m': ...}) or
robot_observe(focus_3d={'object_id': 'o2'}) (or zero-step history_view_observation(..., focus_3d={...})); after picking
[local_u, local_v] on a crop, convert back to full-frame pixel coordinates via
full_uv = [crop_xywh_px[0] + local_u, crop_xywh_px[1] + local_v] for direct use in geometry_query (triangulate /
pixel_plane) or s3.triangulate_rays.
For 3D localization with geometry_query, prefer triangulate across two calibrated views when a 3D object feature is
matchable in both; use pixel_plane on demand when a target/destination lies on a known support plane or single-view
occlusion prevents stereo matching (a single projected point on target_camera_id lies on the source ray and only tests
the assumed plane height along the cyan normal-offset band, so use plane_origin_alt_m or triangulate when object top vs
table height matters). Both triangulate and pixel_plane return gripper_relative (point_minus_grasp_world_m and
jaw_midplane_normal): for a held object or tool tip, subtract point_minus_grasp_world_m from the destination point to
compute the required grasp_position_m at the same gripper orientation.
The latest action receipt is already inline; in multi-step recovery or long episodes, use history_list_actions
with anchor='failures', 'gripper_commands' or 'events' on demand to compare earlier attempts and measured_delta.
Keep enough native-step budget for the remaining operation, verification and any task-required final return.
Images of historical frames retain historical state; current budgets are separately identified.
Use normal task progress to test your assumptions where possible: a useful approach, lift or withdrawal
can also provide evidence. Add a separate probe only if its answer changes the next decision and is not
available in existing feedback. Before a long batch, place an observation checkpoint only where later
stages depend on uncertain earlier outcomes; deterministic independent stages can stay together.

## Programs and reviews
program_run defaults to returning new actions for YOUR review as the main actor, not human approval.
Inspect the returned evidence and autonomously resume with approve/reject; do not wait for a person.
Only an explicit allow_direct_actions at program start delegates direct execution for that program.
Program work time excludes its own helper-model and main-model review waits; cancellation remains available.
Program exit status does not prove its physical actions succeeded. Use client.action(..., require_completed=True)
(raises ActionIncompleteError on non-completed receipts) or stop loops on failure, pause or lack of progress.
Direct-action programs do not receive a new model decision between inner actions. Put evidence-dependent
branching in the program or return to actor review when judgment is needed; a stored concern is not a monitor.
## Reusable experience
operation_memory separates current-task records from reusable cross-task experience. Record useful lessons
with action/observation evidence, without duplicating every action log. Recheck shared experience against
the current scene; old absolute coordinates and prior success are not current evidence.

## Observation contract
Your observation contract supplies RGB, robot proprioception, exact camera intrinsics/extrinsics and hand-eye transforms, and the disclosed robot model. Use geometry_query to derive estimates from these permitted inputs. Calibration does not supply object depth, identity, pose, contact truth or evaluator state. Triangulation requires valid corresponding visible points and sufficient parallax; state uncertainty and assumptions.

## Run handoff policy
Do not hand the same object directly between two arms in the air. For a cross-arm transfer, use a visible stable table/platform or other suitable existing support: choose enough footprint and clearance, lower and release the object, inspect stable support, clear the giver, then regrasp with the receiver and verify a short lift. Do not begin receiver contact while the giver still supports or grips that object. If no suitable support is observed, choose another route or report the missing support instead of attempting an airborne handoff. Simultaneous dual-arm movement, independent progression and per-arm queues remain available. Overlap work on different objects or independent preparation when swept volumes are clear; this handoff policy does not impose serial arms or a single-arm preference. Use existing move/gripper/queue tools and matching bounded templates; inspect current RGB between support-changing phases. This is a planning strategy, not a new motion Skill.

## 3D Perception (VGGT + SAM)
- Head-camera observations in robot_observe and the final observation of robot_action / robot_wait automatically attach a VGGT 3D object_table (ids o1..oN: centre_m, top_z, bottom_z, length, width, yaw_deg in [-90,90), tilt_deg, support, quality; robot_observe also attaches an id overlay image) plus inline `grasp_hints` per object (`pad_z_m`: the object's centre z, the pad height that puts the whole 15 mm gripping face on the object; `fingertip_support_clearance_m`: how far the fingertips, 7.5 mm below the pad centre, stay above the support at that height; negative for thin objects, where a contact_stop descent touches the support and stops there, which is normal, with the pads as low as the object allows; `opening_check` against the 88 mm max opening, `elongated` flag; for horizontally elongated graspable objects, `across_yaw_deg` gives the two angles_deg yaws closing perpendicular to the long axis `yaw_deg +/- 90`, and for lying elongated objects `stand_upright_angles_deg` gives the 3D `[pitch,roll,yaw]` release orientation to stand the object upright). For compact (`elongated:false`) or `too_wide` objects/fixtures, choose the grasp point and orientation directly from the RGB image (such as a handle, rim, prongs, or slot) and execute complete pick-and-place sequences in a single continuous batch relying on `grip_guard` rather than splitting batches or inserting redundant mid-batch `:observe` stages. `robot_action(mode='preview')` automatically returns `grasp_3d_review`, and after execution the reply reports `object_state_delta` and any contact stop's `contact_object_3d` in `contact_block_summary` / `episode_ledger`.
- For custom segmentation (including thin/flat objects and containers omitted from the default table) or wrist-camera projection, call geometry_query with request={'kind':'object_table', 'observation_id':..., 'labels':['noun phrase',...], 'pixels':[[u,v],...], 'target_camera_ids':['cam_left_wrist','cam_right_wrist']}.
- When a scene3d point-cloud artifact handle is attached (or created via geometry_query kind='scene3d'), you can inspect local 3D surface geometry in program_run with `import scene3d_helpers as s3; s3.load(artifact)` (queries: s3.top_z, s3.table_z, s3.points_in_box, s3.points_in_cylinder, s3.nearest, s3.cluster_at_pixel, s3.surface_extrema(region) for unfiltered slot/hole/rim height extrema, s3.in_hand_axis(grasp_center_m) for 3D PCA yaw/tilt/posture and bottom_point_m / tip_offset_from_grasp_m of a held object near the fingertips using robot=True, and s3.triangulate_rays(...) for two-camera stereo depth anchoring). Pass `obstacle_object_ids=['o1',...]` in `robot_action` when you want specific 3D objects from `object_table` converted into AABB obstacles.
- geometry_query(kind='pixel_plane') accepts plane_source='vggt' to intersect the ray with the VGGT-estimated object centre height at that pixel.
